result.title: COMPASS: Cross-modal Observation with Multi-Path Adaptive Stopping and Selection for Early Time Series Classification
result.summary: Early time-series classification (ETSC) balances predictive performance against the amount of observed data. In multimodal settings, modality-associated and fused branches may differ in predictive ability at the same observed prefix, motivating joint decisions about when to stop and which branch should provide the final prediction. We propose COMPASS, a two-stage framework that preserves two modality-associated temporal branches and one fusion branch. The first stage combines cross-modal feature exchange and gated fusion with branch-wise supervision at every prefix. The second stage optimizes a shared four-action controller to continue observation or terminate through one of the frozen branches. Experiments on six physiological and wearable datasets compare COMPASS with multimodal adaptations of five ETSC baselines. COMPASS achieves the best average ranks in accuracy-earliness harmonic mean, AUROC, and earliness within this comparison set. At identical learned stopping times, branch selection improves mean accuracy over fusion readout on five of the six datasets, with gains of 2.35 and 2.16 percentage points on ISRUC-Sleep and UCDDB, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on joint stopping and branch selection for multimodal early time series classification.

AI.brief_summary: COMPASS 针对多模态早期时序分类提出两阶段框架：先保留两个模态关联分支与一个融合分支，做跨模态特征交换、门控融合并逐前缀监督；再学习一个共享四动作控制器，决定继续观察还是经某个冻结分支终止输出。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「继续观察／终止＋选择由哪条分支给出答案」的联合决策，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 时机与依据当前证据选择读出路径提供可核查的机制线索；但工作在生理/可穿戴时序领域，不涉及 latent 推理状态，需自行判断可迁移性。
